subject: Media Literacy
title: Content Moderation Dilemmas
description: A 60-second lesson on Content Moderation Dilemmas.

hook.text: Facebook removes a post about a genocide, then restores it, then removes it again. No one can agree on the right call.

buildup.text: Content moderation decides what billions of people can and can't say online. Platforms make these calls at massive scale.

discovery.text: Moderators must balance free expression against harm — hate speech, misinformation, violence, and harassment.

twist.text: Most moderation is done by AI and underpaid contractors, not careful ethical deliberation. Context is often lost.

climax.text: Platforms have become the largest speech regulators in history, with less transparency than any government.

punchline.text: Unelected companies decide what billions can say. That's power without precedent.

quiz.question: Who primarily performs content moderation on social media platforms?
options: AI systems and underpaid contractors, often lacking context
